sources.title: Retry behavior - AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide
supports: The behaviour the page describes requires opting in with AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026=true until it becomes the default; without it the SDK uses pre-2026 retry behaviour
Retry modes standard and adaptive; legacy is not available in JavaScript; adaptive is not recommended as a general default
AWS_RETRY_MODE / retry_mode and AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS / max_attempts, and the precedence code, environment, shared config file, default
Under the 2026 behaviour: base delay 50 ms for transient errors and 1,000 ms for throttling, cap 20 seconds, full jitter
Under the 2026 behaviour: retry quota of 500 tokens, 14 per transient retry, 5 per throttling retry, 1 restored by a success without retry
Under the 2026 behaviour: DynamoDB and DynamoDB Streams clients default to 4 max attempts with a 25 ms transient base delay
x-amz-retry-after is a delay in milliseconds, clamped between the computed backoff and that plus 5,000 ms
The token budget is typically scoped to a single client instance
sources.note: The page describes the opt-in behaviour only. The pre-2026 numbers in the chapter (100 ms, 500 ms, costs 10 and 5) are from the installed @smithy/core 3.35.2, not from this page.

sources.title: @smithy/core 3.35.2 (installed package source)
supports: submodules/retry/util-retry/retries-2026-config.js: Retry.v2026 is read once at module load from SMITHY_NEW_RETRIES_2026 === "true"; delay 100 or 50, throttling delay 500 or 1,000, costs 5/10 or 14/5
submodules/retry/util-retry/StandardRetryStrategy.js: capacity 500, refusal by error type, attempts, then capacity; retry-after hint clamped to computed delay + 5,000 ms
submodules/retry/service-error-classification: the throttling codes, the transient codes and statuses 500, 502, 503, 504, and that 429 or $retryable.throttling is throttling

submodules/retry/middleware-retry/retryMiddleware.js: amz-sdk-invocation-id and amz-sdk-request headers, $metadata.attempts and totalRetryDelay, a streaming payload is not retried, step finalizeRequest with priority high
submodules/client/middleware-stack/MiddlewareStack.js: the five steps and three priorities
submodules/client/smithy-client/defaults-mode.js and config/defaults-mode: defaultsMode is legacy when unset and then sets no timeout
submodules/client/util-waiter: minDelay, maxDelay, maxWaitTime, exponential backoff with jitter between polls, TimeoutError and AbortError
submodules/config: the Region is read from AWS_REGION or the profile's region; a missing Region throws 'Region is missing'
submodules/endpoints: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_<SERVICE> and AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, and endpoint_url in the shared config file
sources.note: Read from node_modules, the dist-es build. Node.js loads the dist-cjs build of the same version; the tests run against that.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/core 3.978.2 (installed package source)
supports: submodules/client/setFeature.js sets Retry.v2026 when AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026 === "true", at module load
setCredentialFeature records the provider on the credentials' $source

sources.title: @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb 3.1149.0 (installed package source)
supports: runtimeConfig.js: max attempts default 4 only when Retry.v2026, retry mode from AWS_RETRY_MODE or the defaults mode, the request handler is NodeHttpHandler
DynamoDBClient.js: resolveRetryConfig with defaultBaseDelay 25 and defaultMaxAttempts 4 only when Retry.v2026; the plugins the constructor adds to the middleware stack
waiters/waitForTableExists.js: every exception is answered with RETRY; minDelay 20 and maxDelay 120 seconds by default
models/errors.js: the exception classes, their $fault, and that only ReplicatedWriteConflictException declares $retryable

sources.title: @smithy/node-http-handler 4.12.1 (installed package source)
supports: No connection, request or socket timeout unless configured
keepAlive true and maxSockets 50 on the agents it creates
A request that exceeds requestTimeout only logs a warning unless throwOnRequestTimeout is true
An aborted signal rejects with AbortError; ECONNRESET, EPIPE and ETIMEDOUT become TimeoutError
sources.note: The option comments in @smithy/types 4.19.0 (http/httpHandlerInitialization.d.ts) say the same about requestTimeout and throwOnRequestTimeout.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/credential-provider-node 3.972.85 (installed package source)
supports: defaultProvider tries fromEnv, fromSSO, fromIni, fromProcess, fromTokenFile, then the remote provider
fromEnv is skipped when AWS_PROFILE is set, with a warning if static keys are also in the environment
The remote provider is the container endpoint when its environment variables exist, otherwise instance metadata unless AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED is set
Credentials with an expiration are refreshed when less than five minutes remain
sources.note: @aws-sdk/credential-provider-ini 3.973.18 resolves a profile with login_session through @aws-sdk/credential-provider-login; the chain itself has no separate login step, unlike the table in the developer guide.

sources.title: Set credentials in Node.js - AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 Developer Guide
supports: The SDK provides a default credential provider chain in Node.js and stops at the first source that returns credentials
The order of the table: fromEnv, fromSSO, fromIni, fromLoginCredentials, fromProcess, fromTokenFile, fromContainerMetadata, fromInstanceMetadata
The guide recommends short-term credentials
sources.note: The table lists fromLoginCredentials as its own step after fromIni. The installed provider reaches login credentials only through a profile, inside fromIni.

sources.title: Login credentials provider - AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide
supports: aws login writes login_session to the profile and caches short-term credentials under ~/.aws/login/cache
The credentials expire in 15 minutes and are refreshed by the CLI and SDKs for up to 12 hours
SDK for JavaScript 3.x supports it

sources.title: Working with Lambda environment variables - AWS Lambda Developer Guide
supports: AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN are reserved variables that Lambda sets

sources.title: Load credentials for a Node.js Lambda function - AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 Developer Guide
supports: The execution role provides the function's credentials, so the code supplies none

sources.title: Reuse connections with keep-alive in Node.js - AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 Developer Guide
supports: The SDK reuses TCP connections by default
keepAlive can be turned off per client through the request handler's agent

sources.title: Configure maxSockets in Node.js - AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 Developer Guide
supports: maxSockets is 50 when neither a value nor an agent is supplied; requests beyond it are queued
The shorthand requestHandler configuration object, as of v3.521.0

sources.title: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 README, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: The middleware stack and what each of its five steps is for; a request change made in build applies to all retries
In Lambda, one client per service and Region, made outside the handler
Stream outputs carry transformToString and friends, which can be called once
Paginators are async generators; AbortController support and the AbortError

sources.title: SDK Clients - aws-sdk-js-v3 supplemental docs, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: The Node.js request handler uses node:http and node:https even where fetch exists
A streaming response body must be read to the end or destroyed for its socket to be released, because keepAlive defaults to true
When a retryStrategy is given, retryMode and maxAttempts are ignored
cacheMiddleware and its side effect

sources.title: Error Handling - aws-sdk-js-v3 supplemental docs, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: Non-2xx responses are thrown as errors; an unmodeled error is an instance of the service's base exception class
Errors can be told apart by name, by instanceof (the base class overrides Symbol.hasInstance), and by $metadata.httpStatusCode

sources.title: @aws-sdk/lib-storage README, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: Upload's defaults: queueSize 4, partSize 5 MB, leavePartsOnError false
sources.note: The installed Upload.js agrees: MIN_PART_SIZE 5 * 1024 * 1024, MAX_PARTS 10,000, and AbortMultipartUpload on failure unless leavePartsOnError.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb README, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: What marshallOptions convertEmptyValues, removeUndefinedValues, convertClassInstanceToMap, allowImpreciseNumbers and unmarshallOptions wrapNumbers do
For removeUndefinedValues, an item is not itself considered a map: only its attributes are examined
NumberValue for numbers beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
sources.note: The README does not list the defaults in one place. What the document client does with no option set is pinned by test/document.test.ts.

sources.title: @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner README, at tag v3.1149.0
supports: getSignedUrl(client, command, { expiresIn }) and the default of 900 seconds

sources.title: Download and upload objects with presigned URLs - Amazon S3 User Guide
supports: A presigned URL made with temporary credentials expires when the credentials expire, even if a later expiration time was specified
A presigned URL expires at its configured time or when its credentials expire, whichever is first

sources.title: Dual-stack and FIPS endpoints - AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide
supports: AWS_USE_DUALSTACK_ENDPOINT and AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT, both false by default; the request fails where no such endpoint exists

definition.ja: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 で、1 つの API 操作とその入力を表すオブジェクト。クライアントの send に渡して実行する。
definition.en: In the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3, the object that stands for one API operation and its input. It runs when passed to a client's send.

glossary.ja: ミドルウェアスタック

definition.ja: SDK のクライアントが 1 回の呼び出しで順に通す処理の並び。initialize、serialize、build、finalizeRequest、deserialize の 5 つのステップに分かれ、再試行と署名は finalizeRequest にある。
definition.en: The ordered functions an SDK client runs for one call, in five steps: initialize, serialize, build, finalizeRequest, deserialize. Retries and signing live in finalizeRequest.

glossary.ja: 認証情報プロバイダーチェーン

definition.ja: 認証情報を明示しなかったときに、SDK が決まった順に試す取得元の並び。最初に認証情報を返したところで止まる。
definition.en: The sources an SDK tries in a fixed order when no credentials are given in code. It stops at the first one that returns credentials.

definition.ja: 続きを指すトークンやキーを次のリクエストに渡す処理を、非同期のイテレーターとして包んだ SDK の関数。
definition.en: An SDK function that wraps passing the continuation token or key to the next request as an async iterator.

definition.ja: リソースが目的の状態になるまで、間隔をあけて状態を問い合わせ続ける SDK の関数。待つ時間の上限は呼び出す側が決める。
definition.en: An SDK function that polls a resource's state at intervals until it reaches the wanted one. The caller sets how long it may wait.

definition.ja: JavaScript の値と、DynamoDB の型つきの属性値（S、N、M など）を相互に変換すること。lib-dynamodb のドキュメントクライアントが送受信のたびに行う。
definition.en: Converting between JavaScript values and DynamoDB's typed attribute values (S, N, M and so on). The document client in lib-dynamodb does it on every send and receive.

definition.ja: AWS のサービスが返したエラーを表す SDK のクラス。サービスごとの基底クラスを継承し、$fault、$metadata、name を持つ。
definition.en: The SDK class for an error an AWS service returned. It extends the service's base class and carries $fault, $metadata and name.

glossary.ja: リクエストハンドラー

definition.ja: SDK のクライアントの中で、実際に HTTP リクエストを送る部品。Node.js では node:http と node:https を使い、接続の再利用とタイムアウトをここで設定する。
definition.en: The part of an SDK client that actually sends the HTTP request. In Node.js it uses node:http and node:https; connection reuse and timeouts are set here.
